speaker: Unknown
en: Bilal, welcome to the show.
zh: Bilal,欢迎来到节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you, Turner.
zh: 谢谢你，Turner。

speaker: Unknown
en: So good to see you, man.
zh: 见到你真是太好了，兄弟。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's awesome to see you, too.
zh: 见到你也太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm really excited because we haven't really got a chance to sit down and have like a two hour conversation.
zh: 我真的很兴奋，因为我们之前还没怎么有机会坐下来进行像这样两个小时的对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think like ever before.
zh: 我觉得以前从来没有过。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this will be fun.
zh: 所以这会很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think probably the most interesting place to start is you have been investing in what we now call, you know, physical AI for 18 years.
zh: 我想最有趣的切入点可能是，你投资我们现在所说的物理 AI 已经 18 年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were at a pretty large fund, Lux Capital.
zh: 你曾在一家相当大的基金，Lux Capital。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Claude told me $5 billion in AUM.
zh: 我记得 Claude 告诉我资产管理规模是 50 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, $7 billion?
zh: 哦，是 70 亿美元？

speaker: Unknown
en: $7 billion AUM.
zh: 70 亿美元的资产管理规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: You left to start your own fund.
zh: 你离开去创办自己的基金。

speaker: Unknown
en: It wasn't necessarily the hottest thing in the world, but suddenly people will not stop talking about it.
zh: 这本来不一定是世界上最热门的东西，但突然之间人们就停不下来地谈论它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as somebody who's been doing this for a really, really long time, what do most people typically get wrong when they first start to invest in something that's not just software?
zh: 所以作为一个已经做了这件事非常非常长时间的人，当人们刚开始投资于不仅仅是软件的东西时，大多数人通常会把什么搞错？

speaker: Unknown
en: So number one, many thanks to Jensen Huang, who I think in January 2025 put up this chart that now people have seen many times where he says there's, you know, AI, then agentic AI, and then physical AI.
zh: 首先，非常感谢 Jensen Huang,我想他在 2025 年 1 月放出了这张现在人们已经看过很多次的图表，他说有 AI,然后是 agentic AI,然后是物理 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, oh my God, the future is physical AI.
zh: 我当时就想，天哪，未来是物理 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, 18 months ago when I was like starting my conversations with LPs that maybe I should do a fund, there were many LPs who said, we've never done investment in this area, this is capital intensive.
zh: 你知道，18 个月前，当我开始和 LP 们聊也许我该做一只基金的时候，有很多 LP 说，我们从未在这个领域做过投资，这是资本密集型的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I tried to tell them, no, it's not, at least not the way I'm approaching it or the kinds of investments I want to do.
zh: 然后我试图告诉他们，不，不是这样，至少就我的方法或我想做的投资类型而言不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it was an uphill battle because, you know, oh, this is probably only large funds can do this where you can write big checks and hold on to your positions.
zh: 但那是一场艰难的战斗，因为，你知道的，哦，这可能只有大型基金才能做，它们可以开出大额支票并长期持有头寸。

speaker: Unknown
en: That has completely changed in 18 months and everybody wants to invest in it.
zh: 这在 18 个月里彻底改变了，现在每个人都想投资它。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way Jensen describes physical AI, it feels like a little bit more narrow around robotics and autonomy and so on.
zh: Jensen 描述物理 AI 的方式，感觉稍微更窄一些，围绕着机器人和自主性等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: The thesis of my fund is AI and the physical world.
zh: 我的基金的主题是 AI 与物理世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's tremendous innovations happening in AI.
zh: 我认为 AI 正在发生巨大的创新。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we all realize that at this point.
zh: 我想我们到这个时候都已经意识到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: 100 different ways.
zh: 一百种不同的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we want to fund some of those fundamental innovations, but we also believe that AI is going to have a massive impact in real world physical industries, you know, things that we consume, you know, this table, this glass, the food, the energy we consume, the industrially produced products that we have, and so on, defense and all that stuff.
zh: 而且我们想资助其中一些根本性的创新，但我们也相信 AI 将在真实世界的实体产业中产生巨大影响，你知道的，我们所消费的东西，这张桌子、这个杯子、食物、我们消耗的能源、我们拥有的工业生产的产品等等，还有国防之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the mistakes that people make?
zh: 人们会犯什么错误？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, look, number one, there's a lot of very smart people investing in this space and they're coming from different vantage points.
zh: 我是说，你看，第一，有很多非常聪明的人在投资这个领域，他们来自不同的视角。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some people have been doing it for a long time.
zh: 有些人已经做了很长时间了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So clearly they bring that expertise.
zh: 所以很明显他们带来了那种专业经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: They also bring a scar tissue to it.
zh: 但他们也带来了伤疤组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: So sometimes their problem would be that, you know, they've seen too much and they know a hundred ways to fail and that's all they think about.
zh: 所以有时候他们的问题是，你知道的，他们见得太多了，他们知道一百种失败的方式，而他们满脑子想的都是这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they sometimes miss the big idea because they have seen something like it before and they wouldn't do it.
zh: 所以他们有时会错过伟大的想法，因为他们以前见过类似的东西，所以他们不会去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for newer people, you know, go-to-market in these industries is tough.
zh: 而对于较新的人来说，你知道的，在这些行业里进入市场是艰难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Decision-making in your customers is much more complex.
zh: 你的客户的决策要复杂得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: The incentive systems at your customers are not exactly aligned with you.
zh: 你的客户的激励体系和你并不完全一致。

speaker: Unknown
en: They want better products, but they just want to protect their market share more than anything else.
zh: 他们想要更好的产品，但他们最想要的首先是保护自己的市场份额。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've never seen rapid growth and, you know, oligopolies or monopolies.
zh: 他们从未见过快速增长，你知道的，寡头垄断或垄断。

speaker: Unknown
en: That doesn't really happen to them.
zh: 那种事不会真的发生在他们身上。

speaker: Unknown
en: They, you know, they would love to push all the risk to you and you as a young entity might assume all that risk thinking that's what it takes, not realizing that there's not enough at stake for your customer to be there for the long term.
zh: 他们，你知道的，他们很乐意把所有风险都推给你，而作为一个年轻的实体，你可能会承担所有这些风险，以为这就是必要的代价，却没有意识到你的客户没有足够的利益关系来长期陪你走下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you end up sometimes investing in companies that feel like a big idea, but the practicality is missing.
zh: 所以你最终有时会投资于那些看起来像伟大想法的公司，但缺乏实操性。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the things, you know, I talked to LPs about as I was doing fundraising was that, you know, of course, we want to fund big, important ideas, change the world ideas and companies that can become very, very big.
zh: 我在募资时和 LP 们谈过的一件事是，你知道的，当然，我们想资助伟大的、重要的想法、改变世界的想法和能够变得非常非常强大的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And hopefully the entire investment investor ecosystem will want to be a part of that at various stages.
zh: 而且希望整个投资者生态系统的各方都愿意在各个阶段参与其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's not some niche one.
zh: 所以它不是某种小众的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I also said that we want to back founders who understand what it takes to turn a startup into a business.
zh: 但我也说过，我们想支持的创始人，是那些明白把一家初创公司变成一门生意需要付出什么的创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So why is that such a big deal?
zh: 那为什么这是这么大的事？

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, startup, you and I can create a startup during this podcast, probably cost less than $25 to register and we can call it, we're going to go mine on the dark side of the moon and likely get admitted into some accelerator and even get funded.
zh: 你看，初创公司，你我可以在这次播客期间就创建一家初创公司，注册大概花不到 25 美元，我们可以给它起名叫，我们要去月球的暗面采矿，而且很可能被某个加速器录取，甚至拿到融资。

speaker: Unknown
en: Especially with you and my background.
zh: 尤其是凭你和我这样的背景。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I can spin up Claude right now.
zh: 是的，我现在就能把 Claude 拉起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: These guys know how to raise money.
zh: 这些人知道怎么融资。

speaker: Unknown
en: While we're talking, yeah, Claude can go and we'll have a website and a product.
zh: 就在我们聊天的时候，是的，Claude 可以去把一个网站和一个产品做出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: These days, people are saying, can these guys raise money?
zh: 如今，人们在问，这些人能融到钱吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you can raise money, great.
zh: 如果你能融到钱，那很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: People want to fund you, so we can do that.
zh: 人们想要投你，所以我们可以做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the business, business has customers who buy products.
zh: 但生意，生意是有客户购买产品的。

speaker: Unknown
en: When they buy a product, they give you revenues, and the revenues are real only when there's margin associated with that.
zh: 当他们购买产品时，他们会给你收入，而只有当收入伴随着利润率时，收入才是真实的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And going through all those steps is non-trivial.
zh: 走完所有这些步骤绝非易事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's finding a customer on the other side that cares about your product enough to part with real dollars toward you.
zh: 它是要在另一端找到一个足够在乎你的产品、愿意为你付出真金白银的客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in a way that's not just real dollars while they know that you're packaging a dollar with every product you sell to them, but you are actually generating margins and profits on the other side.
zh: 而且不能是他们明知你每卖出一个产品就捆绑了一美元却仍付真金白银的那种，而是你要真正在另一端产生利润率和利润。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a tough ask.
zh: 这是个很高的要求。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the greatest companies that, you know, I've been fortunate to be part of have figured that out.
zh: 而且我认为，你知道，我有幸参与过的那些最伟大的公司都想明白了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as their business starts to grow, they also start to grow the TAM.
zh: 当他们的业务开始增长时，他们也开始把 TAM 做大。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they're turning their startup into a business and the business is becoming bigger and bigger on its own, expanding.
zh: 所以他们把创业公司变成一门生意，而这门生意自己在不断变得越来越大，不断扩张。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the opportunity set in which they're building is becoming bigger.
zh: 而且他们所构建的机会集也在变得越来越大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are the business that I think are just most amazing ones.
zh: 我认为那些才是最了不起的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's basically you need to make sure on day one, or as close to as day one, you can sell a thing profitably.
zh: 所以基本上你需要确保在第一天，或者尽可能接近第一天，你就能有利可图地卖出一样东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're gonna make money.
zh: 你是要赚钱的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe the TAM in a spreadsheet or in a market report can or cannot be big, but it actually has to be large, long-term, whether or not the spreadsheet says it does or not, like it has to materialize over time.
zh: 也许电子表格里的 TAM 或市场报告里的 TAM 可大可小，但它实际上必须足够大，从长期看，不管电子表格怎么说，它必须随时间真正实现出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not so much that you have to start selling day one, you know, you have to do real development, real product work, but you have to understand what it takes, what it takes to sell.
zh: 这并不是说你必须从第一天就开始卖，你知道，你得做真正的研发、真正的产品工作，但你必须明白卖出去需要什么、需要什么才能卖出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I met somebody earlier today
zh: 你知道，我今天早些时候见了一个人

speaker: Unknown
en: Remarkably smart individuals building a research lab in a very important area.
zh: 非常聪明的个体，在一个非常重要的领域建研究实验室。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you reach the point of like, you know, what is your path to turning it into a product that actually people use it?
zh: 但当你谈到类似这样的问题时，你知道，你把它变成一个真正有人用的产品的路径是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: They just haven't thought about it.
zh: 他们根本没想过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they don't see that as a priority, which is fine because they're researchers who are basically doing, you know, research just happens to be inside a company and in today's climate they'll get funded.
zh: 而且他们不认为那是优先事项，这也没问题，因为他们本质上是做研究的，你知道，研究只是碰巧发生在公司里，而且在今天的气候下他们会拿到融资。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think that cannot be your portfolio.
zh: 但我认为这不能是你的投资组合。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, there could be a shot on the goal that, you know, you take in your portfolio.
zh: 我是说，可以有一个射门式的机会，你知道，放在你的投资组合里。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's room for something like that, but that cannot be in a majority of your portfolio.
zh: 有容纳这类东西的空间，但这不能占你投资组合的大多数。

speaker: Unknown
en: You mean as an investment firm?
zh: 你是说作为一家投资机构？

speaker: Unknown
en: As an investment firm.
zh: 作为一家投资机构。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

en: So it's almost like you need to be commercial.
zh: 所以这几乎就是说你必须是商业化的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like the founders need to be commercial and know how to...
zh: 比如创始人必须是商业化的，并且知道怎么……

speaker: Unknown
en: Get customers to pay them for the thing.
zh: 让客户为这个东西付钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Isn't that the purpose of starting a company?
zh: 这不就是创办公司的目的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think so.
zh: 我是说，我觉得是。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, why do we start a company then?
zh: 我是说，那我们为什么要创办公司呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I don't understand if we're not trying to be commercial.
zh: 比如，如果我们不想商业化，我就不理解了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are we professors?
zh: 我们是教授吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are we research?
zh: 我们是做研究的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are we basically saying nobody will give us money in a university, so let me create an alternate form of a university and do research there?
zh: 我们是不是在说没有大学愿意给我们钱，所以让我创建一种大学之外的替代形式，在那里做研究？

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't take me wrong, like Vinod Coastline and others who funded OpenAI, it was not commercial, it was a non-profit.
zh: 别误会我，比如 Vinod Coastline 和其他资助 OpenAI 的人，那不是商业化的，它是非营利组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: Vinod could do that, but Vinod can also give a billion dollars to somebody as a non-profit grant because he wants that to exist.
zh: Vinod 可以那么做，但 Vinod 也可以因为希望某个东西存在而作为非营利资助给某人十亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's very different than necessarily an average VC who's trying to do remarkable investments and make a mark on the world to the extent that Travis Kalanick was saying everyone wants to make a mark on the world.
zh: 这和一个试图做出杰出投资、在世界上留下印记的普通 VC 是截然不同的，就像 Travis Kalanick 所说的，人人都想在世界上留下印记。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we're trying to find amazing individuals who will create real value, who will create real products, who will improve people's lives and who will create products that have economic value in society.
zh: 你知道，我们 trying to find 杰出的个体，他们将创造真正的价值，将创造真正的产品，将改善人们的生活，并将创造出对社会有经济价值的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what we get paid for in return because then society says, thank you for building that.
zh: 而这就是我们因此获得回报的原因，因为社会会说，谢谢你们造出了那个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll give you a lot of money because I think you will continue to add money for a long time to come.
zh: 我们会给你们很多钱，因为我认为你们会在未来很长时间内持续创造钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And hence we will apply a multiple to it that will be pretty high and you can cash out and we will continue with the company going forward.
zh: 因此我们会对它应用一个相当高的倍数，你们可以套现，而我们会让公司继续向前发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you very much.
zh: 非常感谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what we call an exit.
zh: 这就是我们所说的退出。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does that happen a lot, you think?
zh: 你觉得这种情况经常发生吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think so.
zh: 我觉得是。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's flex.one and code TURN for $1,000 on your first $10,000 of spend.
zh: 那就是 flex.one，邀请码 TURN，在你最初的 10,000 美元消费上获得 1,000 美元。

zh: 现在让我们开始吧。

zh: 我认为很多 VC 是被商业化产品所驱动的。

speaker: Unknown
en: VCs are responding to the environment that they're in.
zh: VC 是在回应他们所处的环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: They know what their job is, but sometimes they feel like in the interim, you've got to do what everybody else is doing.
zh: 他们知道自己的工作是什么，但有时候他们觉得在过渡期间，你得做其他人都在做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if everybody else is funding research labs, then maybe I should have a research lab in my portfolio as well.
zh: 如果其他所有人都在投资研究实验室，那也许我也应该在我的投资组合里有一个研究实验室。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then some get carried away.
zh: 然后有些人就走火入魔了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think VCs, investors generally understand that their job is to invest in something that creates long-term real value.
zh: 但我认为 VC，或者说投资者总体上明白，他们的工作是投资于能创造长期真实价值的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people may differ on how long it takes to create that value.
zh: 人们可能在创造这个价值需要多长时间上有分歧。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's okay.
zh: 这没关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, SpaceX is a very old company.
zh: 你知道，SpaceX 是一家很老的公司了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tesla is a very old company.
zh: Tesla 也是一家很老的公司了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like a new company, but it is not.
zh: 它感觉像一家新公司，但其实不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think anybody has a 23-year fund.
zh: 我认为没有人有一支 23 年期限的基金。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think my LPs are willing to give me 23 years.
zh: 我认为我的 LP 不会愿意给我 23 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, maybe if it becomes, you know, at the end of 12 years, if it's starting to look like SpaceX, they'll hold on to it.
zh: 当然，也许到了 12 年期末，如果它开始看起来像 SpaceX，他们会继续持有。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, otherwise, these are 12-year funds.
zh: 但除此之外，这些是 12 年期的基金。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, 10-year funds plus two has become very common.
zh: 实际上，10 年期加 2 年延期已经变得非常普遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe they'll become 15-year funds.
zh: 也许它们会变成 15 年期的基金。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's roughly the timeline that you've got to make your mark on the world with that company.
zh: 但大致上，你必须在这个时间线内用那家公司在世界留下印记。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what's happened over the past couple of years?
zh: 那么过去几年发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if I go back three, four, five years ago, I feel like the mantra was hardware is hard.
zh: 因为如果回到三、四、五年前，我觉得当时的口头禅是硬件很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what's changed that people are now all of a sudden really excited about the category?
zh: 那么是什么改变了，让人们现在突然对这个品类如此兴奋？

speaker: Unknown
en: Hardware is still hard.
zh: 硬件依然很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really encourage people to not let VCs tell you that hardware has become easy.
zh: 我真心劝大家不要让 VC 告诉你硬件已经变容易了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has not.
zh: 并没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, it's become in some ways harder.
zh: 事实上，在某些方面变得更难了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Supply chains in China have been cut off.
zh: 中国的供应链被切断了。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you designed a product here, you could go make it in China.
zh: 如果你在美国这里设计一个产品，你可以去中国制造它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now you have to do everything yourself.
zh: 现在你必须自己做所有事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have firms that are having to, you know, basically reinvent motors and actuators, things that are used to be bought in bulk in China, and we're having to rebuild them here.
zh: 有些公司不得不，你知道，基本上重新发明电机和执行器，这些过去在中国批量采购的东西，而现在我们不得不在这里重建它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: But put that aside, what has changed?
zh: 但把那个放一边，发生了什么变化？

speaker: Unknown
en: Few things have changed.
zh: 有几件事变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is, you know, the founder set that has been attracted to the hardware space is a founder set that Silicon Valley is more familiar with and understand, and that founder set understands how to build fast-moving companies.
zh: 一是，你知道，被吸引到硬件领域的创始人群体，是一个硅谷更熟悉、更能理解的创始人群体，而这个群体知道如何打造快速行动的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've often said that, you know, while technology is a great differentiator for a startup, the real differentiator is the speed.
zh: 我经常说，你知道，虽然技术是初创公司的一个很好的差异化因素，但真正的差异化因素是速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, if you can move fast, you can do amazing things.
zh: 你知道，如果你能快速行动，你就能做成惊人的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can do something that's relatively commodity and build an interesting company because the other players who provide that commodity are stale and are not going to move fast.
zh: 你可以做一些相对同质化的东西，并打造出一家有趣的公司，因为提供那种同质化产品的其他玩家都是僵化的，不会快速行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's like Uber.
zh: 我是说，就像 Uber。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's like a car ride.
zh: 就是，比如打个车。

speaker: Unknown
en: Correct.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's some hundreds of millions of cars around the world.
zh: 世界上有几十亿辆汽车。

speaker: Unknown
en: Correct.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every photo taking app could have created an app that also deletes your photos, but Snapchat did it and they did it fast.
zh: 每一个拍照应用都可以做一个还能删除你照片的应用，但 Snapchat 做了，而且他们做得很快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody could have added filters, but Instagram did it.
zh: 每个人都可以加上滤镜，但 Instagram 做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And eventually everybody tried to, but Instagram had already established its lead and community around it.
zh: 最终每个人都在尝试做，但 Instagram 已经建立了自己的领先地位和围绕它的社区。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in hardware, you know, 18 years ago when I entered venture, we had discovered 18, 20 years ago that there's this whole world of deep tech, clean tech, that, you know, energy is massive.
zh: 但在硬件领域，你知道，18 年前当我进入风险投资时，我们在 18、20 年前就发现有这么一个深度科技、清洁科技的完整世界，你知道，能源是巨大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you know, all of enterprise software business is like three, four trillion dollars of revenue, right?
zh: 比如，你知道，整个企业软件业务的收入大概是 3、4 万亿美元，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Just automotive alone is four trillion dollars of revenue.
zh: 光是汽车行业的收入就是 4 万亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Industrial is another $10, $12 trillion of revenue.
zh: 工业领域又是 10、12 万亿美元的收入。

speaker: Unknown
en: Manufacturing is another.
zh: 制造业又是另一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Construction is another.
zh: 建筑业又是另一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we're talking $40, $30, $40 trillion worth of economy that's available for us to work in.
zh: 我是说，我们说的是 40 万亿、30、40 万亿美元规模的经济体量，可供我们在其中耕耘。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem was that because we did not understand these industries intimately as investors or as founders at that time, we said, who should we fund?
zh: 问题在于，因为我们作为那个时代的投资者或创始人，并不深入了解这些行业，我们会问：我们该投谁？

speaker: Unknown
en: We said, let's find these guys who have 20, 30 years of experience at Shell and GE and BP, who really understand oil and gas and energy and manufacturing, and let's fund them.
zh: 我们说，让我们去找那些在壳牌、GE 和 BP 有 20、30 年经验的人，他们真正懂石油天然气、能源和制造业，我们来投他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that makes sense because they're the experts on the industry.
zh: 是啊，这说得通，因为他们是行业专家。

speaker: Unknown
en: They all know how to navigate.
zh: 他们都知道怎么在行业内周旋。

speaker: Unknown
en: Correct.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they're not founders.
zh: 但他们不是创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't have the founder DNA.
zh: 他们没有创始人 DNA。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't have the entrepreneurial spirit.
zh: 他们没有创业精神。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't move fast.
zh: 他们行动不快。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can't make it and break it.
zh: 他们做不到快速打造、快速试错。

speaker: Unknown
en: They do things the old fashioned way.
zh: 他们用老派的方式做事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And hence, they're no different than the other incumbents.
zh: 因此，他们和其他在位者没有什么不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what happened is that because these industries take a while on its own, by the time they would get to market and market would be ready for them to be there, the incumbents would be like, ah, the market is available, let's go.
zh: 于是发生的事情是，因为这些行业本身就需要一段时间，等他们到达市场、等市场准备好迎接他们时，在位者会说：啊，市场成熟了，我们上吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the incumbents will catch up.
zh: 然后在位者就会追上来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have to move fast.
zh: 所以你必须快速行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to do things slightly more unnatural.
zh: 你必须用稍微不那么常规的方式做事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Starting with, obviously, Elon Musk back in those days and then moving on and, you know, founders of Nest and then Palmer Luckey who created Oculus and, you know, and a bunch of, you know, Aurora and then Applied Intuition and Anduril and, you know, all these companies that we now know about.
zh: 从那个时代的 Elon Musk 开始，然后接着是 Nest 的创始人，然后是创造了 Oculus 的 Palmer Luckey，你知道的，还有 Aurora，然后是 Applied Intuition 和 Anduril，还有，你知道的，所有这些我们现在都知道的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are Silicon Valley folks.
zh: 这些都是硅谷人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They move fast, they hire fast, they raise capital, they deploy capital.
zh: 他们行动快，招人快，融资快，花钱快。

speaker: Unknown
en: They know how to bend the rules.
zh: 他们知道怎么打破规则。

speaker: Unknown
en: They know how to, you know, do things that are not typical for that industry, forward deployed engineers.
zh: 他们懂得如何做那些在那个行业里不寻常的事情，也就是前沿部署工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, you know, and now in physical sciences, it's become a real thing.
zh: 然后，你知道的，现在在物理科学领域，这已经成为一种真实的现象了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the first thing that changed was the quality of the entrepreneur and the type of entrepreneur changed.
zh: 所以第一个变化是创业者的质量和创业者的类型发生了变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think VCs became more comfortable with that.
zh: 我认为风投们对此变得更加适应了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they were no longer talking to stayed, you know, old guard.
zh: 所以他们不再只和那些守旧的老派人物打交道了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second thing that happened was that government was seen as a SBIR mill that would give you small grants that would help you do some development of some really big idea, but never became a customer.
zh: 第二件发生的事情是，政府被视为一个 SBIR 工厂，会给你小额资助，帮助你开发某个非常宏大的想法，但永远不会成为客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really?
zh: 真的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was all, you know, I'm on record talking about this, that this was all bullshit.
zh: 而且这全是，你知道的，我公开谈论过这件事，这全是胡扯。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was, you know, it was a job creation mechanism.
zh: 它是，你知道的，它是一种创造就业的机制。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a few companies that became really, really good at getting SBI mills would get
zh: 而少数那些变得非常、非常擅长拿 SBIR 资助的公司会得到

speaker: Unknown
en: Tens of millions of dollars, in fact, hundreds of millions of dollars in SBIR dollars would just go to them.
zh: 数千万美元，实际上是数亿美元，SBIR 的钱就直接流向了他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are startups?
zh: 这些是初创公司吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are these like incumbent companies?
zh: 还是那种在位的大公司？

speaker: Unknown
en: These are like, I call them SBIR mills.
zh: 这些是，我称之为 SBIR 工厂。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were good at creating proposals and submitting them and getting, you know, there's nothing to, but it's like, you know, I need to do some research.
zh: 他们擅长撰写提案、提交提案并获得，你知道的，没有什么实质内容，但就像是，你知道的，我需要做一些研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me give me some money.
zh: 给我一些钱吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll call it a commercialization effort, but there's no real plan to commercialize.
zh: 我会把它称为一个商业化项目，但实际上并没有真正的商业化计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll get my SBIR one and two and then move on to another topic and SBIR one and two and just keep going.
zh: 我先拿到我的 SBIR 一期和二期，然后转到另一个课题，再拿 SBIR 一期和二期，就这样一直循环下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that was actually the business model was getting government grants essentially.
zh: 所以那实际上就是他们的商业模式，本质上就是拿政府资助。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And kept people afloat for the longest time.
zh: 而这让很多人维持了很长时间的运转。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think thanks to the effort of a lot of founders over the last 10 years, and then frankly, some VCs, you know, I mean, I remember making early defense tech investments 15 years ago and nobody was interested in them.
zh: 然后我认为，多亏了过去十年许多创始人的努力，坦白说还有一些风投，你知道的，我记得 15 年前做早期国防科技投资时，没有人对此感兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then often at these defense tech panels, you know, there'd be the same few of us, Trey and I and a few others were like always on these panels together talking about government needs to change its procurement policies and so on.
zh: 然后在这些国防科技的小组讨论上，你知道的，总是我们同样这几个人，Trey 和我以及其他几个人总是被放在同一个小组里，谈论政府需要改变其采购政策等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that started to change.
zh: 于是情况开始发生变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: That has now become, government's become a massive customer.
zh: 那如今已经变成了，政府成为了一个巨大的客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's a direct customer, but it's also an influencer on the incumbents to say, you need to buy from these guys.
zh: 而且它是一个直接客户，但它也是一个对在位大公司有影响力的角色，会说，你们需要从这些人那里采购。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that has created a very real market.
zh: 这就创造了一个非常真实的市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, government budget is, you know, it's a trillion dollars in defense, but at least a big portion of that is now headed towards these companies.
zh: 我是说，政府预算，你知道的，国防预算是一万亿美元，但至少其中很大一部分现在正流向这些公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now we needed to do a lot more.
zh: 现在我们还需要做更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Trust me, it's still small peanuts relative to the big budget, but certainly even the small peanuts is like big numbers for the startup industry.
zh: 相信我，相对于庞大的预算来说，这仍然只是九牛一毛，但对于初创行业来说，即便是九牛一毛也是很大的数字了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the third thing that happened was that in the world of robotics, everything was very deterministic.
zh: 然后发生的第三件事是，在机器人领域，一切都是非常确定性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by robotics, I mean, broadly speaking, it's, it was, you know, you had to almost hard code.
zh: 我说的机器人，广义上讲，它，你知道的，你几乎必须硬编码。

speaker: Unknown
en: What would you need to do for a robot arm to come in, grab this thing, how much pressure to grab it with and move it here and put it down.
zh: 你需要做什么才能让机械臂过来，抓住这个东西，用多大的压力去抓，把它移到这里然后放下。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like every single potential path that could happen was like literally in the code base.
zh: 所以就像每一个可能发生的潜在路径都真的写在代码库里。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the code base.
zh: 写在代码库里。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's almost like if then statements or something like that.
zh: 几乎就像 if-then 语句之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Relatively speaking, I mean, we're not doing justice to it, but roughly that.
zh: 相对而言，我是说，我们这么说没有完全公平地呈现它，但大致是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it became, you know, probabilistic with AI.
zh: 然后随着 AI 的发展，它变成了，你知道的，概率性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now it is, you know, there's real time models that are looking at, you know, there's, you know, there's obviously vision models that are identifying this and, you know, connecting it.
zh: 而现在，你知道的，有实时模型在观察，你知道的，有，你知道的，显然有视觉模型在识别这个，并且，你知道的，把它连接起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's robotic control models, world models, VLA's.
zh: 然后还有机器人控制模型、世界模型、VLA。

speaker: Unknown
en: All kinds of stuff which is saying, okay, I now know that this is a glass.
zh: 各种各样的东西在说，好的，我现在知道这是一个玻璃杯。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also know that it needs to move there.
zh: 我也知道它需要被移动到那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can take a path to get there.
zh: 我可以规划一条路径到达那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can in real time figure out how to grab this so that I don't crush it.
zh: 我可以实时弄清楚如何抓住它才不会把它捏碎。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all of that stuff became probabilistic.
zh: 而所有这些都变成了概率性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it became much, much more easier to not only solve more interesting problems, but to generalize that solution.
zh: 所以解决更有趣的问题变得容易得多得多，而且还能把那个解法泛化开来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So nobody wants to build a robot or it's not a startup idea to build a robot to pick this up and put it there.
zh: 所以没有人想造一个机器人，或者说造一个机器人来把这个东西捡起来放到那里，这不是一个创业点子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Somebody needs to do that.
zh: 总得有人来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's assume this is a bottling company or a glass filling company, but this is not a very big venture scale business.
zh: 我们假设这是一家装瓶公司或者灌装公司,但这不是一个很大的风投规模的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if I have a model that can do that, but it can do hundreds of other things, now you're doing something very interesting.
zh: 但如果我有一个模型能做这件事,而且它还能做其他几百件事,那现在你就在做一件非常有意思的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is a more venture-like model.
zh: 而这才是更接近风投模式的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that's what you're seeing, especially in physical AI, that people are like, okay, this is very interesting.
zh: 所以我认为这就是你看到的情况,尤其是在物理 AI 领域,人们在想,好吧,这非常有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is not that I can drive a car inside an airport knowing exactly where the lanes are.
zh: 并不是说我能在一座机场里开车,并且精确知道车道在哪里。
